title: Experts disagree on new CI step pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high
context:
Chief architect: This matches the owner's decision to ignore braces by GHSA id, and it adds a check that proves the gate can fail. The flakiness note in the other claim is still true, and the accepted EX-user-flow-writer-7 covers it by requiring the log to name the advisory.

Target: new CI step pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high
- qa-engineer: braces #78 is a high runtime advisory with no patched release, so this step fails on day one unless the exception is recorded in config (pnpm.auditConfig.ignoreGhsas for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). Acceptance: given the lockfile after this change, the step exits 0; given a fixture with a known unignored high advisory, it exits non-zero.
- qa-engineer: Flaky area: the advisory database changes outside our control, so an unrelated PR can turn red the day a new advisory is published. The failure message must name the package and advisory so the cause is obvious, not read as a test flake.
